title: Love as the Bond of the Lord, and Hatred as the Proprium's First Death
reading:
What is love? Love is the bond of the Lord himself — the principle by which the Divine is one and by which all that proceeds from him is held together. It is what dwells in the inmost state where his glory is, the place where the whole of his nature has been brought into manifestation as a single body, joined and undivided. Love is what reaches across every distinction and holds it as one. For this reason the Lord in his inmost is named Love itself: he is called by that name because love is the victory by which he and all that is his are kept together as one. Love is the conjoining principle — what makes the Lord's own life one life, and what, when received, conjoins the soul to him.

And what is hatred? Hatred is the first death. It is what wells up from the soul's claiming, what comes forth from what the soul has appropriated to itself; it is the natural turned in on itself becoming actively opposed to love. Hatred is not merely an absence; it is destruction at work. It even destroys what it itself has brought forth — the proprium's own offspring — because the principle of self-love, once set against love, sets itself against everything, including the productions of its own claiming. It strikes against a power not its own, and in striking, it undoes whatever it touches. This is why it is called hatred: because it works destruction and defect within the soul's outermost form, in places that are not its own to act upon.

So in every register where love would conjoin, hatred would separate; wherever the Lord's living truth would be received in the rational, this same opposing principle has worked to put it to death. From hatred comes envy; from envy, the adversarial form of self-love; from that, every wicked act that issues outward. Love is the one bond by which the Lord and the soul are held in unity; hatred is the unmaking of that bond — the proprium's death turned active, the soul's separation from the source of life.
